newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks at six-yr high in holiday sendoff.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks at six-yr high in holiday sendoff.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed at a six-year high on Monday, edging up on investor hopes that a modest recent rally would resume after the seven-day Chinese lunar new year break starting on Tuesday, brokers said.

The weighted index remained higher throughout the session and closed 31.49 points or 0.43 percent higher at 7,346.88. That surpassed a finish of 7,339.71 on June 5, 1990. The index had closed at 7,315.39 points on Saturday.
Monday's turnover was a relatively brisk T$77.72 billion.
Brokers had expected some profit-taking to hit the market on Monday, the last trading session before the market closes for a seven-day Chinese lunar new year recess.
"The session showed that many investors are reluctant to let the recent gains die out just because the holiday is coming," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst for Yungli Securities.
But in an indication of investor uncertainty about the market's clear direction, trading spread out in various sectors and shareholdings changed hands rapidly, brokers said.
Financials led the way in the first half session but by the end were only 0.55 percent higher due to late profit-taking.
The paper sector emerged to take the lead in late trade, closing 1.64 percent higher with Shihlin Paper gaining T$2.50 to T$84 and Taiwan Pulp and paper rising T$0.50 to T$19.10.
"While investors were unwilling to see the rally end, they also were not entirely secure about leaving their holdings for seven days," Yungli's Chen said.

Brokers said they expected the market to consolidate for a short period after reopening on February 11 before testing a higher upside. A 7,300-7,400 trading range was seen for the post-holiday near term.
